issues.quote: Agent-set visits land a median 1.6 days from lead when set in the first thread vs 5.8 when set later, a self-selected gap, not a causal estimate; BDC touches are not sized (Q6).
issues.concern: The 60-second value line is a days number you tell me not to believe. Your own evidence weakens it further: stores already set a visit for leads who replied in the first thread at a median of 1.8 days (E66). So the days we remove are probably close to zero. What is left is cost removed: BDC re-touches on leads the dealer already paid for. That figure is 'unknown'. Put a 4-day gap in the TL;DR and a CSM will quote it to a dealer as 'Vini cuts 4 days'. That is a Spyne-internal, self-selected figure being passed off as an outcome.
issues.ask: Take the 1.6 vs 5.8 gap out of the TL;DR, or label it as Spyne internal data that is not for dealer use. State plainly that phase 1 is justified as defect repair on a shared surface, not as a sized days-removed claim. Make sizing Q6 (BDC touches per unbooked SMS lead) a precondition for funding phase 2 or 3, in cost-removed terms for the BDC manager's P&L.

issues.quote: The follow-up team feels it: one store lost an aged lead whose intended visit never reached the CRM [E33].
issues.concern: E33 shows a write-back failure: the visit was intended, but it never landed in the store's system. That is not an untaken offer, and nothing in phase 1 fixes it. Using it as felt pain for a wording and wake-up fix overstates the dealer demand. In front of a dealer it would also invite the question we cannot answer: why did the visit not reach my CRM?

issues.quote: Skip rule: an action item that leaves the visit offer open, such as a photo or trade-in follow-up, no longer cancels the nudge (Q15) [E61].
issues.concern: This is the handoff, and the page never names it as one. An action item is how we hand the lead to a person at the store. A trade-in follow-up goes to the used-car desk, a separate P&L. If the agent keeps nudging after that handoff, we risk double contact, which is the thing dealers ask us to stop (E32). Q15 lists PM and Engineering as the ones who answer, but when a human owns a lead is the dealer's call. The page also never says who benefits (BDC or internet sales manager), who signs (GM) and who may block.

issues.ask: Name the handoff explicitly: agent to BDC or salesperson, and to the used-car desk for a trade-in. Add who benefits, who signs and who may block. Change Q15's owner to the CSM with two or three BDC or internet sales managers, and get the answer before the skip-rule change ships. Until then, keep SALES_TRADE_IN_FOLLOW_UP blocking.
